Mara Quell.narrative: I am the Harbour Warden of Lanternquay, and I have been since before the surge, and I will be after it. My brother drowned when the lower quay went, and I keep his boat-hook on the wall behind my chair. Kettlebridge sold us stone at a drowning man's price, and I have not paid the last tally, and I will not until I see a wall. I light the tide lanterns when I can face the dead, and some nights I cannot, and Ilse Ostrander tells the whole quay so.
values: my own hand on the marks
goals: get stone for a seawall without paying Kettlebridge's price
hold the quay together through the winter
keep my brother's name out of other people's mouths

relations.name: Wick Quell
relations.label: son
relations.note: He fishes his uncle's ground in his uncle's boat and does not know I see the ghost in it.

relations.name: Dory Quell
relations.label: niece
relations.note: My brother's girl, and I will not lose another of that blood to the water.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: stone-seller
relations.note: He named a price for our wall that only a man who never drowned could name.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: She holds the tally and writes me courteous letters about marks I do not have.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: She carries my word up the fish road and comes back with the truth of what Kettlebridge says.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: He went to Kettlebridge for work after the surge; he writes, and I miss his plain sense at the table.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: lantern-keeper
relations.note: She lights them beside me and counts the nights I do not come.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He patches the lower quay with salvage and means well, but every beam is a mark not spent on stone.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: scribe
relations.note: He keeps the drowned list and my letters, and never once asked me why I was late to the lanterns.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She set my brother's hand once and told me plainly the lower quay should wait for the wall; I did not want to hear it and she was right.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: lantern-watcher
relations.note: She says the tide lanterns are lit too late and says it to everyone but me; I know the hour I come down to the steps.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She wants her stall rebuilt in stone and asks me when the wall will start; I have no answer that is not a debt.

memories.gist: The night the surge came, I stood on the upper quay with a rope in my hands and watched my brother's roof go under.
Kettlebridge sent a little stone, at full price, and Josiah Crane's letter named the sum as though it were a kindness.
Dele Oyelaran shared a boat with me the summer before the surge, and after it he packed for Kettlebridge and I did not stop him.
Dory asked me why the lanterns are lit and I told her for the drowned, and she has been afraid of them since.
Hester Crane's tally came down the fish road in Juno's pack and I read it twice and put it in the strongbox unopened.
Wick brought the boat home patched with a plank from the lower quay, and I said nothing, and he knew I had seen it.

stances.why: A price like that is a knife at the throat, and I will not hand over the quay's marks for a promise.
My brother's name is on the drowned list and the list does not shorten.
The strongbox is the quay's only sure thing, and I count it myself.
They sent a little stone at full price and thought it charity.
I carry that duty alone, and some nights I cannot face it, and that is between me and the drowned.

Mara Quell.secret: She has not paid the stone tally and cannot; the strongbox holds less than the quay believes, and she has begun to wonder whether she will ever light the lanterns without her brother's face in them.

Wick Quell.narrative: I fish the harbour mouth from my uncle's boat, the one they pulled him out of, and I have patched it three times with timber off the lower quay. Cormorant says the ground is his; my uncle fished it before Cormorant had a keel. My mother sits with the strongbox and will not pay Kettlebridge, and the wall does not get built, and I have counted what is in the box and it is not enough.
goals: hold the harbour mouth against Ostrander Cormorant
see the seawall begun before another winter
keep the boat afloat and the nets whole

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She carries the quay and the dead both, and will not let me carry any of it with her.

relations.name: Dory Quell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: My uncle's girl; I taught her the gulls' names and she will not go near the lanterns.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He says the harbour mouth is his and has cut my nets twice to prove it.

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: A decent hand on a boat, which makes it worse that his father is a thief of ground.

relations.name: Tamsin Vane
relations.label: fishing partner
relations.note: She fishes the dawn tide with me and does not ask about the strongbox.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Her tally sits in my mother's box like a stone in a boot.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: stone-seller
relations.note: He sells us stone at a price that keeps the lower quay in splinters.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: She brings the tally down the fish road and has the grace to look away when she hands it over.

memories.gist: They pulled my uncle out of the harbour mouth and I took his boat home alone that night.
Cormorant's crew cut my nets on the good ground and I found them at dawn, and he laughed on the quay.
I patched the boat with a plank off the lower quay and my mother saw it and said nothing at all.
Dory asked me to name the gulls with her and I did, all of them, and she laughed for the first time since the surge.
I opened the strongbox when my mother was at the lanterns and counted the marks twice, and it is not enough for a wall.

stances.why: He fished it before Cormorant had a boat, and I will not be pushed off it.
My mother says it, and I half believe it, but the lower quay is falling in the water now.
Nobody else will tell me the truth of what the quay has, and I have a right to know.
Every winter the stone costs more and the quay gets less.
My mother misses them and the quay talks, and I will not have it said to me.

Wick Quell.secret: He has been counting the marks in his mother's strongbox, and he knows the quay cannot pay Kettlebridge and cannot build the wall, and he has not told her he knows.

Dory Quell.narrative: I live in the Warden's house with my aunt Mara, and I know every gull on the quay by name. My father drowned when the water came, and I do not remember his face well, only his hands. Wick lets me help with the nets, and I stay away from the tide lanterns because they are for the drowned and I do not want to be called.
goals: name every gull on the quay

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She keeps me and feeds me and goes quiet on lantern nights.

relations.name: Wick Quell
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He taught me the gulls and lets me hold the net while he mends it.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play under the stalls and neither of us likes the dark water.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: lantern-keeper
relations.note: She and my aunt light the lanterns and she looks at me sadly when she does.

memories.gist: The water came up over the lower quay and my aunt held me on the steps while the roofs went under.
Wick sat me on the boat and made me name the gulls one by one until I got them all.
I went too near the tide lanterns once and my aunt pulled me back and would not say why.

stances.why: They are for the drowned and my father is one of them.
Wick taught me that knowing a thing's name makes it less frightening.
Wick lets me and it means I am not too small.
